proposal.reactor_type: PFA coil reactor immersed in a heated aluminum block or oil bath (thermal, non-photochemical)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume / total combined flow rate (10 mL / 1.0 mL·min⁻¹ = 10 min), assuming single homogeneous liquid phase after mixing
proposal.light_setup: None – thermal Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, no photochemical activation required

streams.stream_label: Stream A - Aryl bromide + Pd catalyst
streams.contents: Aryl bromide (0.4 M) + Pd(PPh3)4 (5 mol%, 0.02 M)
Phenylboronic acid derivative (0.48 M, 1.2 equiv) + K2CO3 (0.8 M, 2.0 equiv)

proposal.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume PEEK T-mixer (or micro cross-mixer) upstream of reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Aryl bromide/Pd catalyst stream is combined with the boronic acid/base stream at the point of reactor entry to minimize premature protodeboronation or Pd-catalyst decomposition prior to oxidative addition; immediate mixing followed by heating mimics the near-instantaneous MW dielectric heating of the batch process.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both DMF stock solutions to prevent bubble formation and Pd oxidation
Pre-filter boronic acid/base stream (0.2 µm inline filter) to remove undissolved carbonate particulates
Preheat each stream to 50 °C in a short preheat loop (~1 mL, 1 min) before merging to avoid thermal gradients at the mixer
post_reactor_steps: In-line cooling loop (to ~25 °C) immediately after the reactor coil to quench further coupling/protodeboronation side reactions
Back-pressure regulator (3 bar) to maintain single-phase flow and suppress DMF/H2O off-gassing
Optional in-line liquid-liquid separator to remove aqueous base/boronate residues before collection
Collect biaryl product stream for offline workup (aqueous wash, extraction, and purification)
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling. Batch protocol used microwave dielectric heating for rapid, uniform heating to 50 °C for 10 min, achieving 91% yield with Pd catalyst, base, and DMF solvent. In flow, the MW's instantaneous bulk heating is approximated by pre-heating both streams before merging and passing through a temperature-controlled coil sized to match the 10-min residence time. Because Suzuki couplings are sensitive to Pd catalyst decomposition and boronic acid protodeboronation, minimizing residence time in the mixer prior to reaching reaction temperature is important.

stage_1_preheat.purpose: Bring both streams to reaction temperature prior to mixing

stage_2_reaction.purpose: Primary Suzuki coupling reaction, analogous to 10 min MW batch irradiation

stage_3_cooling_quench.purpose: Halt reaction, prevent Pd black formation, stabilize product prior to workup

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Matches batch microwave irradiation time (10 min) as the primary process variable being translated 1:1, since flow provides continuous but comparably uniform heating.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Selected to give a practically sized reactor volume (10 mL) while keeping a modest total flow (1.0 mL/min) for easy pumping with standard HPLC/syringe pumps.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Directly taken from batch protocol (50 °C); low temperature suggests the arylboronic acid derivative and aryl bromide are highly reactive under Pd catalysis.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Assumed batch volume of ~8 mL for 1.6 mmol substrate, giving ~0.2 M aryl bromide concentration after mixing; original protocol did not specify solvent volume, so this is an engineering assumption for scalable flow translation.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Mild backpressure (3 bar) used to prevent bubble nucleation from dissolved CO2 (carbonate base) and stabilize two-phase mixing without requiring high-pressure hardware, given the low operating temperature (50 °C, well below DMF/H2O boiling points).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Simple PFA coil in a temperature-controlled bath was chosen for compatibility with DMF/water/base mixtures and ease of scale-up; no photoreactor needed since reaction is purely thermal.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA selected for its chemical resistance to DMF, aqueous base, and Pd catalysts, and its practical temperature range compatibility with 50 °C operation.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.5 mm ID chosen to yield manageable coil length (~5.7 m) for 10 mL reactor volume while maintaining laminar flow suitable for Suzuki biphasic mixing.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Derived from residence time (10 min) × total flow rate (1.0 mL/min) = 10 mL, ensuring internal consistency between flow rate and target residence time.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: A low-dead-volume T-mixer or cross-mixer ensures rapid contacting of aryl halide/Pd stream with boronic acid/base stream, minimizing premixing degradation pathways common in Suzuki chemistry.

proposal.literature_analogies: This design follows established continuous-flow Suzuki–Miyaura protocols (e.g., Jensen and coworkers' PFA/stainless-steel coil reactors for Pd-catalyzed couplings, and Org. Process Res. Dev. reports of flow Suzuki couplings using Pd(PPh3)4/K2CO3 in DMF/H2O at 50–100 °C with 5–15 min residence times achieving >85–95% yields), supporting the feasibility of translating a short microwave batch step into an equivalent thermally-controlled flow coil.
safety_flags: DMF is a reproductive toxicant and skin/eye irritant; ensure closed-system operation and fume hood/ventilated enclosure.
Pd catalyst handling requires inert atmosphere precautions to prevent oxidation/deactivation and safe disposal of Pd-containing waste.
Base (K2CO3) slurry may cause line clogging; inline filtration and periodic flushing recommended.
Reaction is mildly exothermic; ensure temperature control loop include failsafe shutoff if coil exceeds 70 °C.
Boronic acid dust is an irritant; use appropriate PPE during stock solution preparation.
Backpressure regulator required to prevent solvent flashing or vapor lock, especially with aqueous/organic mixed solvent.
